questions.explanation: The money multiplier reflects the increased change in money supply that ultimately results from the injection of additional reserves into the banking system. However, the money multiplier differs from the more basic deposit multiplier because banks hold additional reserves, and bank customers convert some portion of checkable deposits into savings deposits or cash. The money that banks do not need to keep in reserve is redirected into financing loans, and the borrowed funds end up on the deposit accounts of other customers. The total amount of new deposits or new money created can be obtained using the money multiplier formula.
